content: 1. Users with an account can opt to receive notifications when specific pages are modified by utilizing the watch feature and their watchlist. MediaWiki does not permit users to claim ownership of pages, but the watchlist feature, combined with the ability to revert edits, allows users to stay engaged with particular pages without granting them full control over the content. 2. Logged-in users can manage which pages they watch by clicking the watch or unwatch link located on the margin of each static page. Clicking watch adds the current page and its associated talk page (or vice versa) to the user's watchlist. Conversely, clicking unwatch removes them. It is not possible to watch a page without also watching its corresponding talk page. 3. When editing a page, the Watch this page checkbox determines whether the page will be added to the watchlist. If the user preference Add pages you edit to your watchlist is enabled, this checkbox will be pre-selected. Unless manually unchecked, the page will be added to the watchlist upon saving the edit. 4. Users can view and manage their watchlist, including mass unwatching of pages, through a dedicated interface accessible via the Watchlist link at the top of the page or by using the URL parameter :Watchlist&magic=yes. 5. The watchlist functions as a personalized recent changes log, displaying updates only for watched pages. It lists pages in reverse chronological order based on the time of the most recent edit. The enhanced watchlist provides additional details, such as the type of edit (minor or major), the time, the editor's username, and the edit summary. It also shows the byte difference (+/-) between the current and previous versions of the page. 6. Minor edits cannot be excluded from the watchlist. In the non-enhanced watchlist, only the most recent edit is displayed, which may obscure prior major changes. To view all changes since the last visit, users must check the page's history. 7. Moving a watched page does not appear in the watchlist. However, both the old and new page names remain on the watchlist after the move. 8. In the Recent Changes, Enhanced Recent Changes, and Related Changes sections, watched pages are highlighted in bold for easier identification. 9. Starting with MediaWiki 1.5, an updated (since my last visit) marker appears on the watchlist, recent changes page, and page history. This marker resets only when the user is logged in while viewing the page. 10. MediaWiki 1.5 introduced an email notification feature (not available on Wikipedia.org) that sends an email when a watched page is edited by another user. Notifications are not repeated until the user views the page while logged in. Minor edits can be excluded from email notifications based on user preferences. 11. Watching a page tracks changes in its wikitext, not the rendered content. Users can also watch templates and their nested templates to monitor changes indirectly. Watching an image or category page is limited to the editable portion, and changes such as adding or removing pages from a category are not reported. 12. Users can watch non-existing pages, which will appear on their watchlist when someone creates them. This is particularly useful for talk pages. To watch a non-existing page, users can follow a broken link to the page and select Watch. 13. The deletion of a watched page does not appear in the watchlist. However, the :Watchlist&magic=yes interface lists all watched non-talk pages, including deleted ones, which are identifiable as non-existent links. Deleted talk pages are not listed separately, making their deletion harder to detect. 14. The Related Changes feature can be used to create custom watchlist-like functionality. By linking pages (e.g., as subpages of a user page), users can monitor changes to those pages and their associated talk pages. However, Related Changes does not detect edits to the page itself or its talk page unless self-links are included. 15. Watching a category or image only tracks changes to the editable portion. Adding or removing pages from a category or modifying an image is not reported in the watchlist. 16. Users can customize the appearance of links to specific pages by defining styles in their CSS. For example, they can change the color, background, or font size of links to emphasize certain pages. This customization works in some browsers, such as Opera, but not in Internet Explorer. 17. Watchlist privacy is maintained, as neither ordinary users nor administrators can view the contents of another user's watchlist or determine who is watching a specific page. However, developers with access to the MediaWiki database can access this information. Public database dumps do not include watchlist data.
